section_summary: This section finishes a translation on Japanese student and civil-servant labor mobilization, then presents translated wartime articles on industry, food, finance, conscription, and conditions in occupied territories. The later pages contain State Department correspondence, file notes, and memoranda about Japan’s postwar economy, especially the scope of economic controls, trade, reparations, and the proposed policy paper SC-101.

subfiles.title: Student and Civil-Servant Labor Mobilization
subfiles.about: A question-and-answer article explains procedures, protections, pay, and assignments for Japanese student and civil-servant labor.
subfiles.summary: The surviving pages discuss simplified student mobilization, relations with ordinary workers, exemptions for ill students, teacher supervision, and compensation. They then describe mobilizing civil servants, particularly technicians for aircraft factories, while retaining their government positions and pay.

subfiles.title: Co-operation Between the Manchurian Heavy Industry Company and the Financial Cliques
subfiles.about: The article describes Japanese financial groups investing in chemical and light-metal enterprises in Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: A table lists four companies, capital amounts, investors, and managers. The article argues that cooperation with Mitsui, Mitsubishi, and Sumitomo will strengthen Manchurian industry.

subfiles.title: Present Condition in the Philippine Islands as Seen from Cabinet Shuffle
subfiles.about: A Japanese article portrays Laurel’s cabinet changes and the Philippines’ shift toward a wartime footing.
subfiles.summary: The article praises Laurel’s leadership and describes ministerial appointments, rice collection, rationing, blackouts, evacuation from Manila, and preparations for air raids. It alleges American-backed guerrilla and espionage activity, then urges political unity and cooperation with Japan. Its claims and rhetoric reflect the wartime Japanese source.

subfiles.title: Formosan Conscription and Wartime Administration
subfiles.about: The article discusses extending conscription to Formosa and reorganizing its administration for defense.
subfiles.summary: The article presents conscription as a sign of Formosa’s integration into the Japanese Empire. It outlines plans for a fortified island and two headquarters covering defense and economic mobilization. The source ends with an appeal to defend the island.

subfiles.title: The Food Problem in North China and Control of Economy
subfiles.about: The article surveys crop prospects and argues for stronger food distribution controls in North China.
subfiles.summary: It reports anticipated harvests in Japan, Formosa, Manchuria, and North China, then gives land and population statistics for five northern Chinese provinces. It attributes urban shortages partly to hoarding and speculation and calls for stronger wartime economic control.

subfiles.title: Arrival and Assumption of Office of Rear-Admiral Minato
subfiles.about: A Shanghai newspaper announces a new Japanese naval attaché and sketches his career.
subfiles.summary: It reports Minato’s arrival as naval attaché in Shanghai and lists earlier naval posts.

subfiles.title: The Future of the War
subfiles.about: The article connects the Leyte battle with Japanese planning, prices, financial controls, and U.S.–Chinese relations.
subfiles.summary: The writer weighs possible outcomes at Leyte and discusses the new Combined Planning Bureau. Later sections consider commodity prices in occupied China, restrictions on Shanghai financial institutions, and the political meaning of General Stilwell’s recall.

subfiles.title: Conscription of Workers
subfiles.about: The excerpt describes Japanese rules for assigning prisoners of war to firms for labor.
subfiles.summary: Firms seeking prisoners of war had to submit plans for lodging, discipline, pay, and medical care.

subfiles.title: National Savings
subfiles.about: Tables report Japanese banknote circulation, savings, and national expenditure.
subfiles.summary: The tables compare annual currency increases and savings figures through 1944.

subfiles.title: Manchukuo State Budget for 1945
subfiles.about: The article reports Manchukuo’s approved general and special budgets for 1945.
subfiles.summary: It gives budget totals and increases over the preceding fiscal year.

subfiles.title: Appointment of General Ando as Governor-General of Formosa
subfiles.about: The article announces Ando’s appointment and reviews his military career.
subfiles.summary: It recounts Ando’s service in China and Formosa and appends a naval appointment notice.

subfiles.title: Personnel Gazette of the Ministry of Interior
subfiles.about: The notice reports Japanese administrative appointments involving Formosa and Hyogo.
subfiles.summary: It outlines Naito’s career and appointment to Formosa’s general affairs administration.

subfiles.title: Letter on Substituting English for Japanese
subfiles.about: Meek adds arguments for making English Japan’s national language after the war.
subfiles.summary: Meek argues that defeat could make Japanese people receptive to a language change as part of postwar reform.

subfiles.title: Reply to P. K. Meek
subfiles.about: Dickover acknowledges Meek’s further arguments about Japan’s national language.
subfiles.summary: Dickover thanks Meek and says his suggestions will be kept in mind.

subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Note on Communist Publications
subfiles.about: The note points to translations on political and economic developments in Japan and occupied areas.
subfiles.summary: It refers readers to a March 31 Chungking despatch filed elsewhere.

subfiles.title: Meeting with Paul H. Johnstone on Japan Studies
subfiles.to: Haley and other State Department officers
subfiles.about: The memorandum records discussion of FEA research and policy assumptions for postwar Japan.
subfiles.summary: Johnstone describes FEA studies and proposes discussing basic assumptions with State Department officers.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Horace B. English’s Letter
subfiles.about: The Navy acknowledges biographical information about a Japanese subject.
subfiles.summary: Forrestal says copies were forwarded to Navy and War Department offices.

subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Note on Economic Conditions
subfiles.about: The note points to a Bern report on economic conditions in Germany and Japan.
subfiles.summary: It identifies the April 19 Bern report and its separate file number.

subfiles.title: Comments of Secretary’s Staff Committee on SC-101
subfiles.about: Lockhart responds to Staff Committee criticism of a proposed economic policy for Japan.
subfiles.summary: He addresses Grew’s proposal for Japanese reconstruction labor and Acheson’s objections to the paper’s generality and treatment of trade. Lockhart argues that SC-101 sets broad, provisional policy pending knowledge of conditions at surrender.

subfiles.title: Abstract of Staff Committee Minutes on SC-101
subfiles.about: An annotated abstract records Staff Committee criticism of SC-101.
subfiles.summary: Acheson calls for concrete recommendations on Japanese industry and trade; Grew raises reconstruction labor, and Holmes finds the presentation superficial. The committee agrees to tell Clayton that the recommendations are too general.

subfiles.title: Japanese Economic Policy Document
subfiles.about: Collado compares Japan policy proposals with German directives and suggests revisions.
subfiles.summary: He recommends clarifying occupation assumptions, the limited place of reparations from current production, and minimum necessary trade. He also discusses living standards, use of local administration, controls on industry and the zaibatsu, and how the paper should advance through committees.

subfiles.title: SC-101: Economic Policy toward Japan
subfiles.about: Lockhart explains the intended scope of the longer-range policy paper.
subfiles.summary: He describes SC-101 as a framework for later, more specific directives.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Redrafting Japan Policy
subfiles.about: Lockhart recommends referring a requested drafting task to Martin.
subfiles.summary: He distinguishes Martin’s prospective presidential paper from the longer-range SC-101 policy statement.

subfiles.title: Request for Foreign Economic Administration Studies
subfiles.about: Corse requests access to studies of Japanese and European economic subjects.
subfiles.summary: The requested FEA reports cover Japanese fuel, food, industry, taxation, and iron ore, along with German property and controls and the Danish economy.
